title: RankSEG-RMA: An Efficient Segmentation Algorithm via Reciprocal Moment Approximation
mechanism: Replace argmax with the decision rule that maximises expected Dice / IoU per image, now O(d) and for non-overlapping classes; the 2026 follow-up (arxiv:2609.38930, RankSEG-DEP) adds local label dependence for small low-contrast objects.
adaptation: Post-process FINAL crack probabilities per cell. It maximises per-image IoU, while our decision metric is pooled IoU, and at 100% labels a val bias adds only about +0.004, so expected gain on test is small; more useful for per-cell benchmark metrics.
min_experiment: No training: RankSEG-RMA (and DEP) vs val-chosen bias on FINAL probabilities. Kill if pooled crack IoU < bias + 0.005 and per-cell IoU not better.
evidence: R: RankSEG almost guarantees improved Dice/IoU over argmax; RMA keeps comparable performance at O(d) (LiTS RankSEG took 16.33 s vs 0.01 s argmax).
prior_overlap: Partial: logit bias tuning was run (+0.014 to +0.023 at 5%, about 0 at 100%); per-image metric-optimal decoding not run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Post-process FINAL crack probabilities per cell; compare against pooled-IoU val bias since RankSEG maximises per-image IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training: RankSEG-RMA on FINAL probabilities; baseline argmax + val-chosen bias. Kill: pooled crack IoU < val-bias + 0.005.
